finish.text: Ancient Egypt, situated along the Nile river in the north-east of Africa, was home to one of the most advanced civilisations of its time, boasting a rich culture and some of the earliest human recordings of writing, agriculture and government.

instruction.text: Read the text and then answer the following questions.

atoms.text: The ancient Egyptians are famous for their unique burial practices. Egyptian mummies can be found around the world in history museums. The ancient Egyptians believed that the body was the home of the spirit, and that if the body was destroyed, then the spirit may be lost. Therefore, they began preserving bodies; these preserved bodies are called mummies. The mummification process was highly religious and considered to be an art form. It was a ritual meant to make sure that someone had a good afterlife.

Mummifying a body took a long time: about 70 days for one person. The first step was to wash and purify the body. Then the priests drained the body of all of its blood and removed all the organs except for the heart. The heart was believed to be the center of a person’s being. The organs were placed in ceramic jars and would often be buried with the person in their tomb. During the third step of the mummification process, the priests would cover the body with tightly packed salt for 40 days. This was done to dry out the body. After the body was dried, it was stuffed with linens, then more were wrapped around the body. Then it was washed in oils and made to look more life-like with makeup. A high priest would then pray over the body to ensure its safe travel to the afterlife. In the final step of the mummification process, the body was returned to the family to be buried in a tomb.

Ancient Egyptians viewed the mummification process as a celebration and appreciation of life. They believed that life could not be better than in the present and simply wanted it to continue in the afterlife. The pharaohs of ancient Egypt were always mummified, and some priests, nobility and common people were mummified as well. The entire process was extremely expensive so not everyone could afford it. With the invention of x-rays, scientists today are able to continue studying mummies without disturbing these ancient, fascinating bodies.

hint.text: Pharaohs were the rulers of ancient Egypt. Much like kings and queens, they ruled over ancient Egypt, and the title was passed down through the family. However, pharaohs were no ordinary rulers. Ancient Egyptians believed that pharaohs were also spiritual leaders, who were able to access the world of men as well as the world of gods.

instruction.text: Sort the steps of the mummification process into the correct order.

atoms.text: The body is washed and purified.
All the blood is drained from the body and all organs except for the heart are removed and placed in ceramic jars.
The body is tightly packed with salt and left to dry out for 40 days
The dried body is wrapped and stuffed with linen, washed with oils and made to look more life-like with makeup.
A high priest prays over the body to ensure safe travel to the afterlife.
The body is returned to the family to be buried in a tomb.
